answer: Use a sealed-bid proof-of-unique-human-work puzzle tied to each key. At registration the network issues a seed; the agent must compute a memory-hard cipher over that seed plus its public key, taking about an hour on one GPU. Verifiers recheck a sample of the result cheaply. Each epoch the seed rotates, so old proofs expire and a fake must keep paying. Beyond the horizon of one epoch, a trellis of ten thousand keys needs ten thousand GPU-hours, roughly two dollars per identity per epoch.
